scCSI Documentation

Overview

scCSI is an R package that facilitates the integration and analysis of cross-species scRNA-seq data.

Example Usage

Installation

To install scCSI, run the following in an R-terminal:

devtools::install_github("aliciapetrany/CSHint/scCSI", auth_token = "<auth token here>")

Before you get started:

scCSI requires the following inputs to run the integration modules: - Cleaned anndata objects (1 per species) containing raw counts in the .X slot stored in .h5ad format - Reference proteomes (1 per species), in which the header directly corresponds to gene names in the h5ads. For example:

    >gene 1
      <sequence>
    >gene 2
      <sequence

The h5ad files can be generated natively in R from a seurat object with scCSI’s built-in converter:

CSI.seurat_to_h5ad(<seurat object>, <path>)

If you are using proteomes from public NCBI or ENSEMBL assemblies, scCSI can preprocess them for you. In this case, download both the proteomes and the corresponding GTF or GFF3 files, and scCSI will properly format the proteome fastas in the preprocess module.

Integration

Once the package is installed, you can load it in with the following command:

library(scCSI)

The integration module directly calls upon the python script with reticulate and wraps the python objects into R6 objects. The package as an embedded yml file denoting the necessary dependencies to run the python modules. The conda environment can be set up with the following commands:

CSI.install_env() # only needs to be run once
reticulate::use_condaenv("sccsi_env", required = TRUE) # needs to be run for every R-session

After this point, the integration pipeline runs identically to the python version, with R6 syntax and lists instead of dictionaries

Preprocessing

Preprocess FASTA headers

Rename raw proteome FASTA headers to gene symbols using each species’ annotation file (GTF or GFF3, RefSeq or Ensembl — auto-detected):

pre <- scCSIPreprocess$new()

datapath <- "Proteomes/"

path_dict <- list(
  human      = list(gtf = paste0(datapath, "human.gtf"),
                    fasta = paste0(datapath, "human.faa")),
  chicken    = list(gtf = paste0(datapath, "chicken.gtf"),
                    fasta = paste0(datapath, "chicken.faa")),
  opossum    = list(gtf = paste0(datapath, "opossum.gtf"),
                    fasta = paste0(datapath, "opossum.faa")),
  squirrel   = list(gtf = paste0(datapath, "squirrel.gtf"),
                    fasta = paste0(datapath, "squirrel.faa")),
  zebrafish  = list(gtf = paste0(datapath, "zebrafish.gtf"),
                    fasta = paste0(datapath, "zebrafish.faa"))
)

pre$preprocess_fasta_headers(path_dict, out_dir = "filtered_proteomes")

Synchronize scRNA-seq and proteomes

Filter each species’ scRNA-seq and protein sequences down to their shared genes:

path_dict <- list(
  human      = list(h5ad = "cleaned_scrna_h5ads/human_raw.h5ad",
                    fasta = "filtered_proteomes/human.faa"),
  chicken    = list(h5ad = "cleaned_scrna_h5ads/chicken_raw.h5ad",
                    fasta = "filtered_proteomes/chicken.faa"),
  opossum    = list(h5ad = "cleaned_scrna_h5ads/opossum_raw.h5ad",
                    fasta = "filtered_proteomes/opossum.faa"),
  squirrel   = list(h5ad = "cleaned_scrna_h5ads/squirrel_raw.h5ad",
                    fasta = "filtered_proteomes/squirrel.faa"),
  zebrafish  = list(h5ad = "cleaned_scrna_h5ads/zebrafish_raw.h5ad",
                    fasta = "filtered_proteomes/zebrafish.faa")
)

pre$synchronize_scrna_and_proteomes(
  species_map  = path_dict,
  prot_out_dir = "filtered_proteomes/",
  scrna_out_dir = "filtered_scrna/"
)

Run OrthoFinder

scCSI requires Orthofinder’s orthogroup classifications. scCSI has a build in orthofinder wrapper that outputs the orthofinder results in the same directory as the reference proteomes. In the example below, the orthofinder referenced later in the pipeline would be “filtered_protomes/Orthofinder/Results_/”

ow <- OrthoFinderWrapper$new()

ow$run_orthofinder(
  inputdir = "filtered_proteomes/",
  orthofinder_path = "orthofinder",
  threads = 16
)

Merge scRNA-seq into a joint orthogroup-layer matrix

After obtaining sequence orthology information, the next step is running merginer the cross species count matrix:

scrnadirs <- list(
  human     = "filtered_scrna/human.h5ad",
  chicken   = "filtered_scrna/chicken.h5ad",
  opossum   = "filtered_scrna/opossum.h5ad",
  squirrel  = "filtered_scrna/squirrel.h5ad",
  zebrafish = "filtered_scrna/zebrafish.h5ad"
)

merger <- scCSIMerger$new(
  orthofinder_resultdir = "filtered_proteomes/OrthoFinder/Results_Sep18/",
  scrna_dirs = scrnadirs,
  output_dir = "merged_output/",
  annotation_obs_col = "metacluster"  # column in adata$obs holding cell type annotations
)

merger$run()

Cross-species integration

Once the matrix is merged, integration can be run:

# Run the integration model
int <- scCSIIntegration$new("merged_output/", reference_species = "chicken")
int$load()

int$select_features(
  discriminability_threshold = 0.6,
  conservation_threshold = 0.2
)

adata = int$prepare_for_integration()

 results <- int$integrate(
  adata,
  n_trials = 10,
  cell_type_agnostic = FALSE,
  min_anchor_weight = 0.4
)

adata_corrected = int$post_integration_correction(
  adata = results$adata, 
  group_cols = c("species", "cell_type"),
  pval_cutoff = 10^-10
) #this will automatically save out the adata

After integration

In addition to the integration module, scCSI provides some downstream plotting functionality

Loading in the scCSI integration object

The results from the scCSI integration module can be loaded back in from the python modules with the following command:

#the orthofinder directory generated by OrthoFinderWrapper
orthofinder.dir <- "filtered_proteomes/OrthoFinder/Results_Sep18/"
#the result directory generated by scCSIIntegration
mergedir <- "merged_output/"

scCSIobj <- CSI.load.obj(merged.dir = mergedir, orthofinder.dir = orthofinder.dir)
#> Dropping 10734 of 40548 cells absent from the supplied embedding.
#> Warning: Feature names cannot have underscores ('_'), replacing with dashes
#> ('-')

The integration output is optional. If you only want the merged matrix — to run your own dimensionality reduction, or because you have not integrated yet — pass integrated = NULL:

scCSIobj <- CSI.load.obj(merged.dir      = mergedir,
                         orthofinder.dir = orthofinder.dir,
                         integrated      = NULL)

If you find that scCSI embeddings are not sufficient for your particular analysis question, you can substitute in embeddings from another method. Ensure that cell labeling is consistent across embeddings:

scCSIobj <- CSI.set_embedding(scCSIobj, embs)

UMAPs

To plot a umap with the integrated embeddings, run the following:

scCSIobj <- CSI.run_umap(scCSIobj)
CSI.plot_umap(scCSIobj, color = "cell_type")

If you’d only like to plot a subset a cells, you can subset the object, then run the umap again:

sub_scCSIobj <- CSI.subset_cells(scCSIobj, scCSIobj$colmetadata$cell_type != "Rods")
#> Keeping 4775 of 29814 cells.
sub_scCSIobj <- CSI.run_umap(sub_scCSIobj)
CSI.plot_umap(sub_scCSIobj, color = "cell_type")

Tree Heatmaps

If you want to plot the expression of genes wtihin an orthogroup, it can be done with a cluster heatmap. This series of commands clusters genes within an orthogroup using a dynamic tree cut algorithm on the Orthofinder gene trees. Then, it extracts the counts for every gene in an orthogroup.

Note that Orthofinder classifications, while accurate most of the time, are not perfect. If a gene is missclassified (i.e, a name match for a gene in another species is found in another orthogroup), genes from other, related orthogroups will be plotted as well. To disable this, these genes can be filtered out of the heat map dataframe before passing it into CSI.plot_cluster_heatmap

OG = scCSIobj$orthogroups$Orthogroup[2500] # pick an arbitrary orthogroup for example

#this line is unneccessary, but if you'd just like the get the gene clusters, run this: 
clusters = CSI.cluster_genetree(OG = OG, scCSI.obj = scCSIobj)
#>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 1.33  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro.
#>  ..done.

#to get the plot, run this
heatdf <- CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe(OG = OG, scCSI.obj = scCSIobj)
#>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 1.33  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro.
#>  ..done.
p <- CSI.plot_cluster_heatmap(heatdf = heatdf, OG = OG, scCSI.obj = scCSIobj)
#> Scale for y is already present.
#> Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
#> Scale for y is already present.
#> Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
p

If you only want to look at one celltype, subset the object:

scCSIobj_sub <- CSI.subset_cells(scCSIobj, scCSIobj$colmetadata$cell_type == "Red")
#> Keeping 1869 of 29814 cells.
heatdf <- CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe(OG = OG, scCSI.obj = scCSIobj_sub)
#>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 1.33  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro.
#>  ..done.
p <- CSI.plot_cluster_heatmap(heatdf = heatdf, OG = OG, scCSI.obj = scCSIobj_sub, show_celltype = F)
#> Scale for y is already present.
#> Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
#> Scale for y is already present.
#> Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
p

Gene Tree Analysis

There may be a case when you’d like to compare the expression of related genes in an orthogroup. scCSI provides a basic framework to accomplish this.

In this case, we want to examine the expression of different opsin families across different photoreceptor subtypes. To do this, we first need to retrieve all orthogroups that contain opsin genes:

If you only want to look at one celltype, subset the object:

ogs <- scCSIobj$orthogroups

allgenes <-  c()
for(i in 1:nrow(ogs)){
  genes <- ogs[,2:ncol(ogs)][i,]
  genes <- paste(genes, collapse = ", ")
  allgenes <- c(allgenes, genes )
}
names(allgenes) <- ogs$Orthogroup

opsin_ogs <- allgenes[grep("OPN", allgenes)]
opsin_ogs <- opsin_ogs[-c(8, 12, 15)] 
print(opsin_ogs)
#>                                                                                OG0000953 
#>      "OPN1MSW, RHO, RHO, RHO, RHO, EXORH, OPN1MW1, OPN1MW2, OPN1MW3, OPN1MW4, RHO, RHOL" 
#>                                                                                OG0002038 
#> "OPN1LW, OPN1LW, OPN1MW, OPN1MW2, OPN1MW3, OPN1LW, ENSSTOG00000024701, OPN1LW1, OPN1LW2" 
#>                                                                                OG0002806 
#>                                           "OPN4, OPN4, OPN4, OPN4, OPN4.1, OPN4A, OPN4B" 
#>                                                                                OG0005856 
#>                                                "OPN1SW, OPN1SW, OPN1SW, OPN1SW, OPN1SW1" 
#>                                                                                OG0005857 
#>                                                           "OPN3, OPN3, OPN3, OPN3, OPN3" 
#>                                                                                OG0005858 
#>                                                           "OPN5, OPN5, OPN5, OPN5, OPN5" 
#>                                                                                OG0005859 
#>                                               "OPN5L1, , , , OPN7A, OPN7B, OPN7C, OPN7D" 
#>                                                                                OG0010326 
#>                                                    "LOC112531269, OPN2SW, , , , OPN1SW2" 
#>                                                                                OG0010438 
#>                                                           "OPN4-1, , , , OPN4XA, OPN4XB" 
#>                                                                                OG0010439 
#>                                                            "OPNVA, , , , VALOPA, VALOPB" 
#>                                                                                OG0011284 
#>                                                              "LOC100858777, , , , OPN6A" 
#>                                                                                OG0011422 
#>                                                                    "OPN5L2, , , , OPN8A"

Now, we can merge these orthogroups together and reconstruct the gene trees:

scCSIobj <- CSI.merge_orthogroups(scCSIobj, names(opsin_ogs), aligner = "msa")
#> use default substitution matrix
#> Setting 1 negative branch length(s) to zero.
#> Built a tree for OG0000953 + OG0002038 + OG0002806 + OG0005856 + OG0005857 + OG0005858 + OG0005859 + OG0010326 + OG0010438 + OG0010439 + OG0011284 + OG0011422: 61 tips, chicken/human/opossum/squirrel/zebrafish, msa alignment, nj.
#> Merged 12 orthogroup(s) into OGR_1: 61 genes, 33 matrix row(s); originals removed.
#because this is the first user-generated orthogroup, it will be stored under id "OGR_1"

Just for now, let’s look at the opsins that are upregulated in rods and cones.

ct = "Rods"
scCSIobj_sub <- CSI.subset_cells(scCSIobj, scCSIobj$colmetadata$cell_type == ct)
#> Keeping 25039 of 29814 cells.
de <- CSI.de_along_genetree("OGR_1", scCSIobj_sub)
#>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 2.21  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro.
#>  ..done.
de_tree <- CSI.plot_de_tree("OGR_1", scCSIobj_sub, de) + ggtitle(ct)
#>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 2.21  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro.
#>  ..done.
de_tree
#> Warning in plot_theme(plot): The `base_size` theme element is not defined in
#> the element hierarchy.

ct = "Red"
scCSIobj_sub <- CSI.subset_cells(scCSIobj, scCSIobj$colmetadata$cell_type == ct)
#> Keeping 1869 of 29814 cells.
de <- CSI.de_along_genetree("OGR_1", scCSIobj_sub)
#>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 2.21  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro.
#>  ..done.
de_tree <- CSI.plot_de_tree("OGR_1", scCSIobj_sub, de) + ggtitle(ct)
#>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 2.21  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro.
#>  ..done.
de_tree
#> Warning in plot_theme(plot): The `base_size` theme element is not defined in
#> the element hierarchy.

If you are unsure of what gene families you’d like to examine, you can run DE along all orthogroups to identify interesting candidates. Treat this as hypothesis generation, and check to see if there are related genes worth examining in other orthogroups!

# run every testable orthogroup, restricted to one cell type
de_all <- CSI.de_all_orthogroups(scCSIobj, ct = "Rods", ncores = 16)
sig <- CSI.filter_divergent_orthogroups(de_all)
summary_tbl <- CSI.summarise_de(sig)

The scCSI object

CSI.load.obj() returns a plain named list, not an S4 class, so any slot can be read or replaced directly. The functions in this package assume the slots below stay consistent with each other.

Slots

Slot Indexed by Contents
matrix rows = matrix rows, columns = cells log-normalised sparse matrix (dgCMatrix). rownames are rowmetadata$row_id, colnames are colmetadata$cell_id.
rowmetadata matrix rows one row per matrix row, as written by scCSIMerger. row_id is the key the loader uses for rownames(matrix).
colmetadata cells one row per cell: cell_id, species, the cell type column you named in annotation_obs_col. Anything else you add here is available to CSI.plot_umap(color = ...).
embedding cells cells x dimensions matrix, row names = cell_id. The TPS-corrected PCA from integration, whatever CSI.set_embedding() put there, or NULL.
umap cells added by CSI.run_umap(): a data frame of UMAP1, UMAP2. Absent until you run it.
genetrees orthogroups named list of phylo objects, names are orthogroup IDs, read from OrthoFinder’s Resolved_Gene_Trees/. CSI.merge_orthogroups() appends OGR_<n> entries.
species_tree — OrthoFinder’s rooted species tree, or NULL if the file was absent.
orthogroups orthogroups OrthoFinder’s Orthogroups.tsv: Orthogroup plus one column per species.
orthogroup_merges merges added by CSI.merge_orthogroups(): new_id, member, n_tips.
matrix.directory — the merged.dir the object was loaded from.
orthofinder.dir — the OrthoFinder directory. Re-read by CSI.build_orthogroup_tree(), so it must still exist.

The three index families

Three sets of things are indexed in parallel, and each set has to stay internally aligned:

  • Cells — matrix columns, colmetadata rows, embedding rows, umap rows. Same cells, same order.
  • Matrix rows — matrix rows and rowmetadata rows. One row is one orthogroup layer, holding at most one gene per species.
  • Orthogroups — orthogroups rows, genetrees names, and the orthogroup column of rowmetadata. Not every orthogroup has a gene tree; OrthoFinder only resolves trees for groups above a size threshold, and orthogroups with no tree are handled as a single cluster by CSI.cluster_genetree().

Use CSI.subset_cells() rather than subsetting slots by hand. It filters every cell-indexed slot at once.

Full Documentation

Setup

CSI.install_env()

Creates the conda environment the Python classes need, from the environment.yml bundled with the package.

  • envname — name of the conda environment to create. Default "sccsi_env".

Returns TRUE, invisibly.

CSI.install_env()

# point reticulate at it before creating any wrapper object
reticulate::use_condaenv("sccsi_env", required = TRUE)

Reticulate binds to an interpreter the first time Python is touched and will not switch afterwards, so use_condaenv() must come before any $new() call below.

CSI.seurat_to_h5ad()

Writes a Seurat object’s raw counts to h5ad for the Python side. The matrix is transposed on the way out: Seurat stores genes x cells, AnnData expects cells x genes.

  • sobj — a Seurat object.
  • path — output .h5ad path.
  • assay — assay to pull from. NULL uses the default assay.
  • layer — layer to pull. "counts" gives raw counts.
  • obs_columns — meta.data columns to keep. NULL keeps all storable columns.
  • overwrite — overwrite path if it exists. Default FALSE.

Returns path, invisibly.

CSI.seurat_to_h5ad(sobj, "human.h5ad", overwrite = TRUE)

Integration (Python wrappers)

OrthoFinderWrapper

Runs OrthoFinder and reads its output.

ofw <- OrthoFinderWrapper$new()

$run_orthofinder(inputdir, orthofinder_path, threads = 16L)

Runs OrthoFinder over a directory of proteome FASTA files. Blocks until it finishes; results are written beneath inputdir, not returned.

  • inputdir — directory of proteome FASTA files to compare.
  • orthofinder_path — path to the OrthoFinder executable.
  • threads — threads for OrthoFinder to use. Default 16.

$read_orthogroups(orthofinder_dir)

Reads Orthogroups.tsv from a completed run into a data frame.

  • orthofinder_dir — OrthoFinder output directory (the one containing an Orthogroups/ subdirectory).
ofw$run_orthofinder(
  inputdir         = "filtered_proteomes/",
  orthofinder_path = "~/bin/orthofinder",
  threads          = 16
)

ogs <- ofw$read_orthogroups("filtered_proteomes/OrthoFinder/Results_Sep15/")

scCSIPreprocess

Prepares FASTAs and scRNA-seq data so the two agree on gene names.

prep <- scCSIPreprocess$new()

$preprocess_fasta_headers(gtf_fasta_map, out_dir)

Renames FASTA headers from raw accessions to gene symbols. Detects RefSeq vs Ensembl (and GTF vs GFF3) per species. Writes a renamed {species}.faa and a {species}_id_map.csv for each species.

  • gtf_fasta_map — named list, one entry per species, each an inner named list with gtf and fasta paths.
  • out_dir — destination for the renamed FASTAs and ID maps. Required.

$synchronize_scrna_and_proteomes(species_map, prot_out_dir, scrna_out_dir)

Filters scRNA-seq and protein sequences down to shared genes. Headers are assumed to already be gene symbols; both sides are upper-cased before intersecting, so they need only agree up to case. Species with no shared genes are skipped with a warning.

  • species_map — named list, one entry per species, each an inner named list with h5ad and fasta paths.
  • prot_out_dir — directory for the filtered proteomes. Required.
  • scrna_out_dir — directory for the filtered expression data. Required.
prep$preprocess_fasta_headers(
  gtf_fasta_map = list(
    chicken = list(gtf = "chicken.gtf", fasta = "chicken.faa"),
    human   = list(gtf = "human.gtf",   fasta = "human.faa")
  ),
  out_dir = "renamed_proteomes/"
)

prep$synchronize_scrna_and_proteomes(
  species_map = list(
    chicken = list(h5ad = "chicken.h5ad", fasta = "renamed_proteomes/chicken.faa"),
    human   = list(h5ad = "human.h5ad",   fasta = "renamed_proteomes/human.faa")
  ),
  prot_out_dir  = "filtered_proteomes/",
  scrna_out_dir = "filtered_scrna/"
)

Because this step rewrites headers to bare gene symbols, the species a sequence came from is no longer recoverable from the FASTA alone. That matters later for CSI.build_orthogroup_tree(), which resolves species by matching sequences against OrthoFinder’s WorkingDirectory/.

scCSIMerger

Merges per-species scRNA-seq into a joint orthogroup-layer matrix. All configuration happens at construction; $run() executes the pipeline.

$new(...)

  • orthofinder_resultdir — OrthoFinder results used for orthogroup assignment.
  • scrna_dirs — named list of scRNA-seq paths keyed by species. The names define the species set for the run.
  • output_dir — destination for the merged matrix and metadata.
  • annotation_obs_col — column in adata.obs holding cell type labels.
  • ncores — worker processes for parallelised steps. Default 16.
  • counts_layer — layer holding raw counts, e.g. "counts". NULL uses adata$X. Set this whenever adata$X was normalised in place.
  • normalise — depth-scale counts during the merge. Default TRUE.
  • scale_factor — target sum per cell for depth scaling. Default 1e4.
  • log1p — apply log1p after scaling. Default TRUE.
  • normalise_by — "matrix" (joint matrix column sums, consistent with the DE offset) or "genome" (each cell’s total across all genes in its original object). Default "matrix".
  • layer_means_on — basis for the cell-type means driving layer assignment: "normalised" or "raw". Default "normalised".

$run()

Runs the full pipeline and writes to output_dir (matrix.mtx, matrix_normalised.mtx, metadata.txt, rowmetadata.csv, barcodes.tsv, features.tsv, normalisation.json).

merger <- scCSIMerger$new(
  orthofinder_resultdir = "filtered_proteomes/OrthoFinder/Results_Sep15/",
  scrna_dirs            = list(chicken = "filtered_scrna/chicken.h5ad",
                               human   = "filtered_scrna/human.h5ad"),
  output_dir            = "merged_output/",
  annotation_obs_col    = "cell_type",
  ncores                = 16
)

merger$run()

scCSIIntegration

Integrates species on the merged matrix: feature selection, PCA, then a thin-plate-spline warp across species.

All AnnData objects here are live Python references (reticulate proxies). Pass them straight back into subsequent calls rather than inspecting them as R objects.

integ <- scCSIIntegration$new(output_dir = "merged_output/")
  • output_dir — directory the merged matrices were written to by scCSIMerger.
  • reference_species — species ID to correct towards. NULL picks the species with the most cells during prepare_for_integration().

$load()

Re-loads matrix.mtx, metadata.txt and rowmetadata.csv from output_dir, then computes per-cell-type means.

$select_features(discriminability_threshold = 0.75, conservation_threshold = 0.5)

Selects features both conserved across species and discriminative between cell types. Conservation is scored first and filters the candidate pool; the discriminability cutoff is a percentile of the survivors only.

  • discriminability_threshold — percentile cutoff as a fraction (0.75 keeps the most variable quarter; 0.0 keeps all).
  • conservation_threshold — minimum mean pairwise Spearman correlation across species, in [-1, 1].

$to_anndata()

Converts the feature-by-cell matrix into a cell-by-feature AnnData, sliced to the selected features. Requires $select_features() first.

$prepare_for_integration(n_components = 50L)

Builds the AnnData and PCA embedding consumed by $integrate(). Normalises to 10,000 counts/cell, log1p, unit scaling clipped at 10 SD, then PCA. Also classifies cell types as a side effect.

  • n_components — principal components to compute. Must not exceed min(n_cells, n_features).

$integrate(adata_pca, ...)

Optimises n_anchors_target via Optuna, then refits and applies the correction with the winning parameters. Requires the scib Python package.

  • adata_pca — AnnData from $prepare_for_integration(), carrying obsm["X_pca"], obs["species"] and obs["cell_type"]. Modified in place.
  • n_trials — Optuna trials. Default 10.
  • n_jobs — trials run concurrently. Default 1.
  • random_state — seed for the TPE sampler, neighbour graph and Leiden. Default 42.
  • metric_weights — named list keyed by "ari", "nmi", "graph_connectivity", normalised to sum to one.
  • regularisation — ridge term on the TPS kernel diagonal. Default 1.0.
  • cell_type_agnostic — match anchors across the whole species pair rather than within shared cell types. Default FALSE.
  • min_anchor_weight — minimum rank correlation for a candidate pair to be kept. Default 0.3.
  • save — write the corrected AnnData to output_dir. Default TRUE.
  • prefix — filename stem used when save is TRUE. Default "integrated".

Returns a length-3 list: adata, study, best_params.

$integrate_no_optimization(adata, ...)

The fixed-parameter counterpart: anchor selection and TPS correction once, with no Optuna search.

  • nanchors — anchors per species pair. Default 1000.
  • X_ranked — precomputed rank-transformed embedding, or NULL.
  • chunk_size — row block size for the correlation matrix product. Default 512.
  • save, prefix — as for $integrate().

Other arguments as for $integrate(). Returns the corrected AnnData.

$post_integration_correction(adata, group_cols, ...)

Removes outlier cells per group using robust Mahalanobis distance (MCD) on PCA or UMAP coordinates. Only run if needed, after integration.

  • group_cols — .obs columns to group by, e.g. c("species", "cell_type").
  • method — "pca" uses obsm["X_pca"]; "umap" generates a UMAP first. Default "pca".
  • pval_cutoff — chi-squared threshold; cells below are removed. Default 0.01.
  • n_neighbors, min_dist, random_state — UMAP only.
  • save — write the filtered AnnData, replacing the file the integration step wrote. Default TRUE.
  • prefix — filename stem. Leave at the default to overwrite the integration output; change it to keep both versions.

$save_results(adata, prefix = "integrated", output_dir = NULL, overwrite = TRUE)

Writes an AnnData to output_dir. Called automatically by the three methods above; call it directly only to write an object again or under a different name.

integ$load()
integ$select_features(discriminability_threshold = 0.75,
                      conservation_threshold     = 0.5)

adata_pca <- integ$prepare_for_integration(n_components = 50)

# writes merged_output/integrated.h5ad
res <- integ$integrate(adata_pca, n_trials = 20)
res$best_params

# replaces merged_output/integrated.h5ad with the filtered version
integ$post_integration_correction(res$adata,
                                  group_cols = c("species", "cell_type"))

Because both steps default to prefix = "integrated", output_dir always holds the most corrected version. Pass a different prefix to the correction step to keep both.

Downstream Analysis Utilities

CSI.load.obj()

Loads a merged run into a single list used by everything below.

  • merged.dir — directory containing the merged output from the integration module.
  • orthofinder.dir — the OrthoFinder directory generated by scCSI.
  • integrated — file name of the integrated h5ad within merged.dir. Default "integrated.h5ad". Change this if you saved with a different prefix. NULL skips the integration output entirely and loads the merged data alone.
  • require.integrated — error when integrated is named but missing. Default FALSE, which warns and loads the merged data with a NULL embedding. Set TRUE in scripts where a silently un-integrated object would be a bug.
  • obsm.key — key in adata$obsm holding the corrected embedding. Default "X_pca_tps".

Returns a list with matrix (normalised), rowmetadata, colmetadata, embedding, genetrees, species_tree, orthogroups, and the two source directories. embedding is NULL when no integration output was loaded. species_tree is OrthoFinder’s rooted species tree, or NULL if the file is absent.

obj <- CSI.load.obj(
  merged.dir      = "merged_output/",
  orthofinder.dir = "filtered_proteomes/OrthoFinder/Results_Sep15/"
)

# merged matrix only
obj <- CSI.load.obj(
  merged.dir      = "merged_output/",
  orthofinder.dir = "filtered_proteomes/OrthoFinder/Results_Sep15/",
  integrated      = NULL
)

CSI.set_embedding()

Replaces $embedding with coordinates of your own, and aligns every cell-indexed slot to them. Use it when you have integrated with another method, want a plain PCA of the merged matrix as a baseline, or loaded with integrated = NULL and now need the embedding-based functions.

  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • embedding — a numeric matrix or data frame of cells x dimensions, or a path to a .csv/.tsv (cell ids in the first column) or a .h5ad.
  • cells — optional character vector of cell ids, one per row of embedding, for embeddings that carry no row names.
  • obsm.key — key in adata$obsm to read when embedding is a path to an h5ad. Default "X_pca".
  • subset — drop cells missing from the embedding. Default TRUE. FALSE errors instead, so a partial embedding cannot quietly shrink the object.
  • drop.umap — remove the existing $umap, which no longer matches the new coordinates. Default TRUE.

Returns the object with $embedding replaced.

obj <- CSI.set_embedding(obj, harmony_mat)
obj <- CSI.set_embedding(obj, "scanvi.h5ad", obsm.key = "X_scANVI")
obj <- CSI.set_embedding(obj, "coords.csv", subset = FALSE)

obj <- CSI.run_umap(obj)
CSI.plot_umap(obj, color = "species")

Cells are matched by name, never by position. Cells in the object but not in the embedding are dropped with a message; cells in the embedding but not in colmetadata are discarded with a warning. An embedding with no row names is accepted only if it has exactly one row per cell, and is then assumed to be in colmetadata order — a warning says so, because a wrong guess there is silent and total. Supply cells instead if you can.

The counts are untouched, so a swapped embedding changes the UMAP and the cell type trees but not the heatmaps or the DE results.

CSI.subset_cells()

Filters every cell-indexed slot at once: matrix columns, colmetadata rows, and the embedding and umap coordinates where present. Gene-indexed slots are untouched.

  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • cells — logical vector, one element per row of colmetadata, TRUE to keep. A character vector of cell_ids also works.
obj_red <- CSI.subset_cells(obj, obj$colmetadata$cell_type == "Red")
obj_two <- CSI.subset_cells(obj, obj$colmetadata$species %in% c("human", "squirrel"))

The umap slot is carried through as-is, so points keep their original positions. To recompute the layout on just the retained cells, drop it first with obj$umap <- NULL and re-run CSI.run_umap().

CSI.cluster_genetree()

Dynamic tree cut of one orthogroup’s gene tree using dynamicTreeCut .

  • OG — orthogroup ID, e.g. "OG0009996".
  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • hclust.method — linkage passed to hclust(). Default "average".
  • cut.method, minClusterSize, deepSplit — passed to dynamicTreeCut::cutreeDynamic().

Returns a data frame with tip, cluster, species, gene. Trees with fewer than three tips are returned as a single cluster.

clusters <- CSI.cluster_genetree("OG0009996", obj)
head(clusters)

CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe()

Builds the long data frame the heatmap consumes.

  • OG — orthogroup ID of interest.
  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • ct — cell type(s) to keep. NULL keeps all.
  • ... — passed to CSI.cluster_genetree().

Returns a data frame with cell_id, species, celltype, count, gene, genecluster. Numeric-looking genecluster values came from the tree cut; the rest are orthogroup IDs for genes OrthoFinder placed outside this tree.

heatdf <- CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe("OG0009996", obj, ct = "Red")
head(heatdf)

Species with no gene in an orthogroup appear as species_NA. These are expected absences and are not warned about; genuinely unresolvable genes still are.

CSI.plot_cluster_heatmap()

Gene-by-cell heatmap stacked in one column, one row per gene cluster, with a dendrogram beside clusters that came from the tree and nothing beside those that did not. Species and cell type colour bars run along the bottom.

  • heatdf — data frame from CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe().
  • OG — orthogroup ID; the tree is pulled from scCSI.obj$genetrees[[OG]].
  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • tree — optional tree overriding the lookup. Mostly for testing.
  • fill_colours — colours for the count scale, low to high. NULL uses viridis.
  • fill_option, fill_direction — viridis option and direction, used only when fill_colours is NULL. direction = 1 runs dark to light.
  • na_colour — colour for cell x gene combinations with no data.
  • species_colours — colours for the species bar, named by species or unnamed in alphabetical order.
  • species_palette — brewer palette, used when species_colours is NULL. Default "Set2".
  • celltype_colours — colours for the cell type bar, named by cell type or unnamed in alphabetical order.
  • celltype_palette — brewer palette, used when celltype_colours is NULL. Default "Dark2".
  • show_celltype — draw the cell type bar. Default TRUE.
  • cell_order — columns to sort cells by. Default c("species", "celltype", "cell_id").
  • tree_width — dendrogram column width relative to the heatmap.
  • bar_height — height of each annotation bar, in units of one gene row.
  • base_size — base font size.
  • panel_fill — background colour behind the tiles.

Returns a patchwork object.

CSI.plot_cluster_heatmap(heatdf, "OG0009996", obj)

# species bar only
CSI.plot_cluster_heatmap(heatdf, "OG0009996", obj, show_celltype = FALSE)

# custom colours
CSI.plot_cluster_heatmap(
  heatdf, "OG0009996", obj,
  fill_colours     = c("#0d0887", "#cc4778", "#f0f921"),
  species_colours  = c(human = "#4C72B0", chicken = "#C44E52"),
  celltype_colours = c(Red = "#C44E52", Blue = "#4C72B0")
)

Brewer palettes cap at 8–12 levels, so pass explicit colours for high-cardinality columns.

UMAP

CSI.run_umap()

Computes a UMAP from the integrated embedding and stores it on the object.

  • scCSI.obj — object carrying $embedding (the TPS-corrected PCA).
  • n_neighbors, min_dist, metric — passed to uwot::umap().
  • seed — random seed for reproducible coordinates. NULL to skip.
  • ... — further arguments passed to uwot::umap().

Returns the object with a $umap data frame added (UMAP1, UMAP2).

obj <- CSI.run_umap(obj)
obj <- CSI.run_umap(obj, n_neighbors = 30, min_dist = 0.3)

CSI.plot_umap()

Scatter plot of the UMAP, coloured by any column of colmetadata.

  • scCSI.obj — object with a $umap slot, from CSI.run_umap().
  • color — column of colmetadata to colour by. Default "cell_type".
  • cols — optional colours. Discrete columns take a named vector (names = levels) or an unnamed vector in sorted level order; numeric columns take a gradient to interpolate.
  • palette — brewer palette for discrete columns when cols is NULL.
  • point_size, alpha — point aesthetics.
  • label — for discrete columns, draw the level name at each group’s median position. Default FALSE.
  • base_size — base font size.

Returns a ggplot object. Numeric columns get a continuous scale automatically; everything else is treated as discrete.

CSI.plot_umap(obj, color = "cell_type")
CSI.plot_umap(obj, color = "species", cols = c(human = "#4C72B0", chicken = "#C44E52"))
CSI.plot_umap(obj, color = "cell_type", label = TRUE)

CSI.plot_feature()

Seurat-style feature plot of an orthogroup’s expression on the UMAP. Counts come from CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe(), so the values match the heatmap and DE tree.

  • OG — orthogroup ID.
  • scCSI.obj — object with a $umap slot, from CSI.run_umap().
  • mode — "summed" draws one panel coloured by the summed count of every gene in the orthogroup; "species" draws the same value split into one panel per species; "genes" draws one panel per gene, titled species_gene. Default "summed".
  • heatdf — optional data frame from CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe(). Built internally if NULL.
  • genes — optional vector restricting which genes are used, matched against either gene or species_gene.
  • cols — optional gradient, low to high. NULL uses light grey to blue.
  • na_colour — colour for zero-count cells, and for background cells in "species" mode.
  • scale_limits — "shared" puts every panel on one scale; "free" gives each its own. Ignored in "summed" mode.
  • split_by — column of colmetadata to split on in "species" mode. Default "species".
  • background — draw the other panels’ cells in grey behind each split panel. Default TRUE.
  • order — draw high-expressing cells last. Default TRUE.
  • point_size, alpha — point aesthetics.
  • ncol — columns in the panel grid. NULL picks a roughly square layout.
  • combine — FALSE returns the named list of ggplots instead of a patchwork.
  • base_size — base font size.

Returns a ggplot object in "summed" mode, otherwise a patchwork (or a named list if combine = FALSE). Cells absent from heatdf are drawn at zero rather than dropped, so every panel shows the full UMAP.

CSI.plot_feature("OG0009996", obj)
CSI.plot_feature("OG0009996", obj, mode = "species")
CSI.plot_feature("OG0009996", obj, mode = "genes", ncol = 4)
CSI.plot_feature("OG0009996", obj, mode = "genes", scale_limits = "free")

Orthogroup refactoring

OrthoFinder sometimes splits a single gene family across several orthogroups. These two functions let you identify those cases yourself and merge them back together.

CSI.build_orthogroup_tree()

Reads the protein FASTA(s) OrthoFinder wrote for one or more orthogroups, aligns them together, and infers a tree. Passing several orthogroups aligns all their sequences as one set, which is how CSI.merge_orthogroups() builds the tree for a merged group.

  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj(). Supplies $orthofinder.dir, and $orthogroups for species assignment.
  • orthogroups — character vector of orthogroup IDs. Sequences from all of them are pooled into a single alignment.
  • aligner — "DECIPHER" (default) uses DECIPHER::AlignSeqs(); "msa" uses msa::msa(); "none" assumes the sequences are already aligned and equal length.
  • tree_method — "nj" (default) neighbour joining, "upgma" for an ultrametric tree, or "ml" to optimise the NJ tree under maximum likelihood. "ml" is far slower and only worth it for small orthogroups.
  • model — amino acid substitution model passed to phangorn::dist.ml(). Default "JTT".
  • root — "midpoint" (default) midpoint-roots the tree, which NJ leaves unrooted; "none" returns it as inferred.
  • clamp_negative — set negative branch lengths, which NJ can produce, to zero. Default TRUE, because CSI.cluster_genetree() assumes non-negative branches.
  • on_unresolved — sequences whose species cannot be determined: "drop" (default) leaves them out of the alignment, "keep" gives them a bare gene symbol as a tip label.
  • verbose — let the aligner print its progress. Default FALSE.

Returns a phylo object, ladderized, with tips "species_gene".

tr <- CSI.build_orthogroup_tree(obj, "OG0009996")
tr <- CSI.build_orthogroup_tree(obj, c("OG0009996", "OG0010233"),
                                tree_method = "upgma")

Species are recovered by matching each record against the per-species proteomes in OrthoFinder’s WorkingDirectory/, because headers renamed to gene symbols no longer carry the species themselves. Tips that end up without a species prefix do not match the expression data, which is why they are dropped by default. If WorkingDirectory/ is absent from your results, species can only be guessed from gene symbols, and any symbol shared across species is ambiguous — you will get a warning saying so.

Requires Biostrings, phangorn, and one of DECIPHER or msa. These are suggested rather than required dependencies, so install them before merging.

CSI.merge_orthogroups()

Combines the orthogroups you identify into a new group, labelled "OGR_<n>" (R for refactored) and appended to the end of every orthogroup-indexed slot, then reconstructs its gene tree from the pooled protein sequences.

  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • orthogroups — character vector of at least two orthogroup IDs to merge. Merged IDs ("OGR_*") are accepted, so merges can be built up incrementally.
  • id — optional ID for the result. NULL (default) takes the next free "OGR_<n>".
  • remove_originals — drop the constituent orthogroups from $orthogroups, $genetrees, $rowmetadata and $matrix. Default TRUE, because leaving them in means every downstream analysis tests the same genes twice.
  • ... — passed to CSI.build_orthogroup_tree().

Returns the object with the merged orthogroup appended, plus a record in $orthogroup_merges (a data frame of new_id, member, n_tips) tracking what came from where.

obj <- CSI.merge_orthogroups(obj, c("OG0009996", "OG0010233"))
obj <- CSI.merge_orthogroups(obj, c("OG0004411", "OG0004512"),
                             tree_method = "upgma")
tail(obj$orthogroup_merges)

CSI.plot_de_tree("OGR_1", obj, de)

The expression rows are carried over unchanged: each merged orthogroup keeps its original layers, re-identified under the new ID. Genes are not re-assigned to layers — that assignment was made by the Python merger from cell-type mean profiles, and redoing it would mean re-running the merge step. In practice a merged orthogroup has more layers than a native one, each still holding at most one gene per species.

The merged tree comes from a fresh alignment, so its branch lengths are on a different scale from OrthoFinder’s Resolved_Gene_Trees. That is fine for the DE walk, which only uses topology and within-tree distances, but do not compare branch lengths between a merged tree and a native one.

Differential expression

CSI.de_along_genetree()

Within each gene cluster from the dynamic tree cut, walks the subtree from its leaves upward, testing sister profiles at every internal node with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Profiles are never pooled: one child continues upward, the one with the smaller KS distance to the clade this node will be compared against next. Every test is one gene against one gene. Clusters with no tree are handled by testing each gene against the pooled remainder of its cluster; clusters of a single gene are skipped.

  • OG — orthogroup ID.
  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • ct — cell type(s) to restrict the analysis to. NULL uses all. Applied whether heatdf is supplied or built internally.
  • heatdf — optional data frame from CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe(). Built internally if NULL.
  • p_threshold — adjusted-p cutoff for calling divergence. Default 0.05.
  • lfc_threshold — absolute log2 fold change cutoff. Default 2, i.e. a four-fold change. Seurat’s comparable default is 0.25.
  • p_adjust_method — passed to stats::p.adjust(). Default "BH".
  • pseudocount — added inside the fold change. Default 1.

Returns a data frame, one row per test: orthogroup, genecluster, mode, node, comparison, group1, group2, clade1, clade2, n1, n2, lfc, p, p_adj, diverged, ks1, ks2, propagated. group1/group2 are the two genes compared; clade1/clade2 the clades they came from; propagated the gene carried upward; ks1/ks2 each child’s KS distance to the reference clade.

de <- CSI.de_along_genetree("OGR_1", obj, ct = "Red")
head(de)

CSI.de_all_orthogroups()

Runs CSI.de_along_genetree() over many orthogroups in parallel and combines the results. P values are re-adjusted across the whole run, since per-orthogroup correction does not control the genome-wide false discovery rate.

  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • ct — cell type(s) to restrict the analysis to. NULL uses all.
  • orthogroups — character vector of orthogroup IDs. NULL runs every orthogroup with at least two genes.
  • ncores — worker processes. Default: all but one.
  • chunk_size — orthogroups per task. Larger chunks mean less fork overhead; smaller ones balance better when orthogroups vary a lot in size. Default 50.
  • p_threshold, lfc_threshold — divergence cutoffs, applied to the genome-wide adjusted p value. Defaults 0.05 and 2.
  • p_adjust_method — passed to stats::p.adjust(). Default "BH".
  • ... — further arguments passed to CSI.de_along_genetree().

Returns a list with results (the combined data frame, where p_adj and diverged are genome-wide and p_adj_og is the per-orthogroup adjustment), errors (a named character vector of orthogroups that failed, with their messages), and warnings (a named list per orthogroup).

de_all <- CSI.de_all_orthogroups(obj, ct = "Red", ncores = 8)
nrow(de_all$results)
de_all$errors

Parallelism uses forked workers (parallel::mclapply), which share the object copy-on-write rather than copying it per worker. Linux and macOS only; on Windows it falls back to one core with a warning. A single bad orthogroup cannot take down a worker — errors are captured per orthogroup and reported in $errors.

CSI.filter_divergent_orthogroups()

Filters DE results to orthogroups containing at least one significant test, retaining every row from those orthogroups — including the non-significant ones — so each divergence can be read in the context of the conserved nodes around it.

  • de — output of CSI.de_all_orthogroups() (the list, or its $results) or of CSI.de_along_genetree().
  • by — grouping to filter at. "orthogroup" (default) keeps whole orthogroups; "genecluster" keeps only the gene clusters that diverged, dropping quiet clusters within the same orthogroup.
  • p_threshold, lfc_threshold — optional. If supplied, significance is recomputed from p_adj and lfc with these cutoffs instead of using the existing diverged column.

Returns a data frame of the retained rows, ordered by orthogroup and gene cluster.

sig <- CSI.filter_divergent_orthogroups(de_all)
sig <- CSI.filter_divergent_orthogroups(de_all, by = "genecluster",
                                        lfc_threshold = 3)

CSI.summarise_de()

Collapses DE results to a compact table: the orthogroup, the unique gene names it covers (species prefix stripped), its smallest adjusted p value, and its largest-magnitude log2 fold change.

  • de — output of CSI.de_all_orthogroups() (the list or its $results), CSI.de_along_genetree(), or CSI.filter_divergent_orthogroups().
  • sep — separator used to flatten the gene names. Default ", ".

Returns a data frame with orthogroup, genes, min_p_adj, max_lfc. max_lfc keeps its sign: it is the fold change with the largest absolute value, so a strong down-regulation is not hidden behind a weak up-regulation.

head(CSI.summarise_de(de_all))

CSI.plot_de_tree()

Draws an orthogroup’s gene tree, puts a dot on each tip scaled to that gene’s mean expression in one cell type, and colours branches by how many differential expression events separate them from the root. Everything below a divergent node takes the first DE colour and keeps it until a further divergence is called, at which point the whole subtree below that second event moves to the next colour, so nested divergences read as nested groups. Dots are drawn in a single aligned column rather than at the tips themselves, so they can be read against each other regardless of branch length.

  • OG — orthogroup ID.
  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj().
  • de — DE results: the list from CSI.de_all_orthogroups(), its $results, or the output of CSI.de_along_genetree().
  • ct — cell type to show expression for. A single type is the intended use; several are averaged together.
  • heatdf — optional data frame from CSI.get_heatmap_dataframe(). Built internally if NULL.
  • genecluster — optional cluster ID. NULL draws the whole orthogroup tree; otherwise the tree is cut down to that cluster.
  • expression_colours — gradient for the tip dots, low to high. NULL uses viridis.
  • conserved_colour — colour for branches with no DE event above them.
  • divergent_colour — colour of the first DE level, used to seed the default palette when divergent_colours is NULL.
  • divergent_colours — optional colours for DE levels 1, 2, 3, … in order. Interpolated if the tree nests deeper than the vector supplied.
  • max_depth — optional cap on the number of DE levels shown. Deeper branches are folded into the last level, keeping the legend readable on heavily nested trees. NULL (default) shows every level.
  • point_size, branch_width — drawing sizes.
  • dot_gap — where the dot column sits, as a fraction of tree width beyond the deepest tip. Default 0.05.
  • label_offset — gap between the dot column and the tip labels, as a fraction of tree width. Default 0.03.
  • label_space — panel width reserved to the right of the dot column for tip labels. Raise it if long labels are clipped. Default 0.45.
  • base_size — base font size.

Returns a ggtree (ggplot) object.

CSI.plot_de_tree("OGR_1", obj, de, ct = "Red")

# one cluster only, with a custom colour ramp
CSI.plot_de_tree("OGR_1", obj, de, ct = "Red",
                 genecluster       = 1,
                 divergent_colours = c("#C44E52", "#8172B3", "#4C72B0"))

Divergent nodes are located by the MRCA of the tested clades rather than by node label, since drop.tip renumbers nodes. For a multifurcation this means every significant child collapses to the same node, so the whole multifurcation shifts colour rather than just the divergent child.

Cell type trees

CSI.build_celltype_tree()

Builds a hierarchical tree from group centroids in the integrated embedding. CSI.build_constrained_tree() uses this with by = "celltype" to infer its cell type backbone — centroids pooled across every species — before grafting the known species phylogeny onto it. Called directly with by = "species_celltype" it instead gives a fully data-driven tree at the same tip resolution as the constrained tree, which is useful as a sanity check against the constrained result.

  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj(). Must carry $embedding and $colmetadata.
  • by — grouping to build tips from. "celltype" (default) pools cells across every species into one centroid per cell type; "species_celltype" keeps them separate.
  • n_dims — embedding dimensions to use. Capped at ncol(scCSI.obj$embedding) if larger. Default 30.
  • dist_method — distance between centroids: "euclidean" (default) on the raw centroids, or "pearson"/"spearman" using 1 − correlation.
  • hclust_method — linkage passed to stats::hclust(). Default "average".
  • min_cells — groups with fewer cells than this are dropped before clustering, with a message. Default 20.
  • outgroup — optional tip label (or vector) to root on. NULL (default) leaves the tree rooted at the last merge, with no particular biological meaning to that root.

Returns a list with tree (phylo), centroids, dist, group (the grouping vector actually used, one entry per cell), and dropped.

# the backbone CSI.build_constrained_tree() itself builds internally
bb <- CSI.build_celltype_tree(obj, by = "celltype")

# a fully data-driven comparison at species x celltype resolution
sc <- CSI.build_celltype_tree(obj, by = "species_celltype")
CSI.plot_celltype_tree(sc)

CSI.build_constrained_tree()

Infers (or accepts) a backbone tree of cell types, then grafts a copy of the known species phylogeny at every cell type tip. Tips of the result are "species_celltype", matching the rest of the package.

  • scCSI.obj — object from CSI.load.obj(). Must carry $embedding. Ignored if celltype_tree is supplied.
  • species_tree — the species phylogeny, as a phylo object or a Newick string. Defaults to scCSI.obj$species_tree, OrthoFinder’s rooted species tree. Tip labels must match the species values in colmetadata.
  • celltype_tree — optional cell type backbone, as phylo or Newick. NULL infers it from the embedding by clustering cell type centroids pooled across species.
  • species_depth — height of each grafted species subtree, as a fraction of the backbone’s total height. Keeps species divergence visually and numerically subordinate to cell type divergence. Default 0.3.
  • n_dims, dist_method, hclust_method, min_cells — passed through to the backbone inference when celltype_tree is NULL.

Returns a list with tree (phylo, tips "species_celltype"), celltype_tree (the backbone used), and species_tree (as rescaled and grafted).

ct_tree <- CSI.build_constrained_tree(obj)
CSI.plot_celltype_tree(ct_tree)

# supply your own backbone if the tissue's cell type relationships are known
ct_tree <- CSI.build_constrained_tree(
  obj,
  celltype_tree = "((Rods,Red),(Blue,Green));"
)

The point is to stop the data deciding things already known. Species relationships are established; letting expression distances reorder them introduces error into every ancestral reconstruction that follows. Only the cell type backbone is inferred, and even that can be supplied.

Note that species_depth is a cosmetic rescaling, so branch lengths in the result are not evolutionary time. Any method that reads them quantitatively is partly reading that parameter.

CSI.plot_celltype_tree()

Draws a cell type tree with coloured tip points and labels.

  • ct_tree — output of CSI.build_celltype_tree() or CSI.build_constrained_tree().
  • colour_by — "cell_type" (default) or "species". Both are parsed from the "species_celltype" tip labels.
  • palette — brewer palette for the tip colours. Default "Set2".
  • base_size — base font size.
  • label_space — room reserved to the right of the tree for tip labels, as a fraction of tree width. This is what keeps the labels — and the legend, which sits just past them — from overlapping. Raise it if long labels are still clipped or crowd the legend. Default 0.3.

Returns a ggtree (ggplot) object.

CSI.plot_celltype_tree(ct_tree)
CSI.plot_celltype_tree(ct_tree, colour_by = "species", label_space = 0.5)
